# Simulation

## Overview

ChromSimPipe simulates with the Hansen lab's
[polysim](https://github.com/ahansenlab/polysim_bootcamp) package: a 3D polymer
on polychrom / OpenMM (GPU) coupled to a 1D model of cohesin loop extrusion.
It is pinned to one commit in `envs/cohesin_sim.yml`.

Each `simulateShard` SLURM job runs `scripts/run_simulation_shard.py` for one
locus, condition, replicate and shard. It:

1. Reads the condition's cohesin parameters, the `polysim:` settings and the
   locus' oriented CTCF sites from `configs/parameters.py` (the locus comes from
   `$CHROMSIM_LOCUS`, set by the workflow).
2. Tiles the locus along one long chain (see [Tiling](#tiling)).
3. Seeds numpy and C `drand48` from the shard seed. polysim draws every cohesin
   decision from `drand48()` and never seeds it, so without this every shard
   would replay one random sequence.
4. Calls `polysim.sim3d.run()`, which writes `blocks_*.h5` (each saved frame
   also carries the cohesin bonds as `SMCs`) into
   `output/loci/{locus}/sims/{params_name}_ctcf-{sample}_rep{N}_shard{M}/`.

A `preparePolysim` job imports polysim once before the shards start, so its
Cython module (`LEF_Dynamics.pyx`) is compiled once rather than by every GPU
job at the same time.

## Cohesin and CTCF

Cohesin rings (loop extrusion factors, LEFs) bind, extrude a loop with two
legs moving apart, and unbind. Oriented CTCF sites stop a leg arriving from the
correct side.

```
5'─────────────────────────────────────────────────────3'
          ↑ cohesin loads (uniformly, unless `loading:` is set)
          ├──►  ◄──┤  (two legs extrude outward)
          │          │
          ▼          ▼
    +CTCF◄          ►−CTCF  (each stops the leg arriving from inside the loop)
```

| Event | Setting | Default |
|-------|---------|---------|
| Number of cohesins | chain length / `separation` | one per 240 kb |
| Leg step | probability `vlef` per LEF timestep | 0.0025 (one step per 400 timesteps) |
| Unbinding | probability 1 / `lifetime` per timestep | 75,000 timesteps, so ~190 kb extruded per leg |
| Stall at CTCF | probability `ctcf_capture` per encounter | 0.5 |
| Stalled lifetime | × `life_boost_stalled` when both legs are stalled | × 4 |

Orientation comes from the FIMO motif strand in the `orientCTCF` output
(`scripts/extract_ctcf_sites.py`): a **+** site stops leftward-moving legs (the
left anchor of a loop), a **−** site stops rightward-moving legs (the right
anchor). Convergent pairs (+ … −) therefore hold loops. These map onto
polysim's `ctcf_left` and `ctcf_right` stall arrays.

## The 3D polymer

Each monomer is one `resolution` (1 kb) of chromatin. Forces:

| Force | What it models | Setting (`polysim:`) |
|-------|---------------|----------------------|
| Backbone bonds and bending | Chromatin fibre | `bond_wiggle` 0.1, `angle_k` 0.05 (flexible) |
| Soft repulsion | Excluded volume | `repel` 3 kT |
| Spherical confinement | Nuclear volume | `density` 0.3, `confinement_k` 1 |
| Cohesin bonds | A harmonic spring between the two legs of each cohesin | `smc_bond_wiggle` 0.2, `smc_bond_dist` 0.5 |

One block is `poly_steps_per_block` (33) Langevin steps of `dt` 40 fs, which the
polysim bootcamp equates with about 20 ms; cohesin moves on the same block
clock (one leg step per 1 / `vlef` blocks). A conformation is saved every
`saveevery` (50) blocks, after `initsteps` cohesin-only steps and an optional
unsaved polymer equilibration (`initskip`, extended by polysim to at least one
cohesin lifetime).

::: {.callout-note}
The simulation runs on a GPU. The SLURM job requests 1 GPU, 4 CPUs and 60 GB
RAM, set under `set-resources:` in `profiles/<site>/config.yaml` (on Longleaf:
`l40-gpu,volta-gpu,gpu` partitions, `qos: gpu_access`). All `simulateShard`
jobs (loci × conditions × replicates × shards) can run in parallel.
:::

## Beyond CTCF and uniform cohesin

Each condition can switch on more of polysim's model (full list in
[Configuration](configuration.qmd#every-condition-option), examples in
[Perturbation recipes](recipes.qmd)):

| Option | Layer | What changes | Implemented through |
|--------|-------|--------------|---------------------|
| `separation: none` | cohesin | no cohesin at all | polysim `sep=None` |
| `ctcf_capture: {min, max}` | cohesin | each CTCF site's stall probability follows its peak signal | polysim per-site stall probabilities |
| `loading` | cohesin | cohesin loads preferentially at peaks | polysim's per-bead loading array |
| `pausing` | cohesin | cohesin steps more slowly at peaks | polysim's per-bead pause array |
| `sticky`, `sticky_cross` | polymer | beads under a factor's peaks attract each other | polysim `monomer_types` + `interaction_matrix` |
| `attraction_energy` | polymer | all beads attract weakly (compaction) | polysim `attraction_energy` |

polysim's own settings fill loading and pausing uniformly; ChromSimPipe
passes the profiles by wrapping polysim's `extrusion.build_lef_arrays` for
the duration of one run (`scripts/sim_features.py`), without changing
polysim. Sticky sites and `attraction_energy` use polysim's
heteropolymer force (`heteropolymer_SSW`) instead of the default repulsion,
so compare them against a condition with `attraction_energy: 0`.

`bash sweep_1d.sh` runs the cohesin layer alone (no polymer, CPU only) for a
grid of settings, as a cheap screen
([recipe](recipes.qmd#a-1d-screen-before-3d-runs)).

## Tiling

To get statistically robust contact maps from one locus, copies of it are
placed end to end on one long chain, separated by `tiling.padding` monomers on
each side, as many as fit in `tiling.chain_size` (70,000) monomers. The 1,960 kb
chr1 locus gives 28 copies of 2,500 monomers. Each copy folds independently,
and after the simulation the contact maps of all copies are averaged into one
locus-sized map. See Yang et al. 2023 *Nat Commun* for why this is valid.

## Entry point

```bash
CHROMSIM_LOCUS=chr1_fig1 python scripts/run_simulation_shard.py \
    --condition cond1_baseline \
    --replicate 1 \
    --shard-index 0 \
    --n-shards 2 \
    --output output/loci/chr1_fig1/sims
```

Arguments come from Snakemake wildcards. Each job writes to:

```
output/loci/{locus}/sims/{params_name}_ctcf-{sample}_rep{replicate}_shard{shard}/
├── params.json        # all parameters, for reproducibility
└── blocks_*.h5        # saved conformations (+ cohesin bonds)
```

After all shards finish, `mergeShards` concatenates them:

```
output/loci/{locus}/sims/merged_{params_name}_ctcf-{sample}_rep{replicate}/
├── params.json
└── blocks_*.h5        # full trajectory (all shards combined)
```
